question: ABCD is a trapezium in which BC || AD and AC = CD. If and angle BAC = 94° , then what is the measure of ∠ACD (in degree)? angle ABC = 36°
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In ΔABC, sum of angles is 180° ⇒ ∠BCA = 180° − (94° + 36°) = 50°.

Since parallel lines BC and AD have alternate interior angles, ∠CAD = ∠BCA = 50°.

As AC = CD, angles opposite to equal sides are equal ⇒ ∠ADC = ∠CAD = 50°.

In ΔACD, sum of angles is 180° ⇒ ∠ACD = 180° − (50° + 50°) = 80°.

**∴ The correct answer is 80°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ In trapezium ABCD, sides BC || AD

⇒ AC = CD

⇒ ∠BAC = 94° and ∠ABC = 36°

**Calculations:**

⇒ The sum of angles in ΔABC is 180°.

⇒ ∠BCA = 180° − (∠BAC + ∠ABC)

⇒ ∠BCA = 180° − (94° + 36°) = 180° − 130° = 50°

⇒ Since BC || AD, AC acts as a transversal line making the alternate interior angles equal.

⇒ ∠CAD = ∠BCA = 50°

⇒ In ΔACD, it is given that the side lengths AC and CD are equal.

⇒ Angles opposite to equal sides are equal, thus ∠ADC = ∠CAD = 50°.

⇒ The sum of interior angles in ΔACD is 180°.

⇒ ∠ACD = 180° − (∠CAD + ∠ADC)

⇒ ∠ACD = 180° − (50° + 50°) = 180° − 100° = 80°

**∴ The correct answer is 80°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Trapezium

A trapezium is a quadrilateral with exactly one pair of parallel sides. The consecutive interior angles located between the parallel sides are always supplementary.

Alternate Interior Angles Theorem

When a transversal intersects two parallel lines, each pair of alternate interior angles is equal (often visualizing a Z-shape).

Isosceles Triangle Theorem

If two sides of a triangle are equal in length, then the angles opposite to those sides are also perfectly equal. The converse property stands true as well.
